feed.title: ADP Warns of Cooling Labor Market While Its Own Business Feels the Chill
feed.summary: ADP's latest figures indicate a significant slowdown in the U.S. labor market, with its "pays per control" growing only 1% in fiscal 2026 and projecting 0-1% for 2027. feed.title: In 1939, As War Broke Out In Europe, He Told His Broker: 'Buy Me $100 Of Everything Below $1 A Share.' Over The Next 7 Decades, John Templeton's Philosophy That 'The Time Of Maximum Pessimism Is The Best Time To Buy' Made Him One Of The Wealthy
feed.summary: In 1939, John Templeton, then 26, borrowed $10,000 and invested $100 in each of 104 distressed stocks trading below $1 a share on the NYSE and AMEX, despite the outbreak of World War II. He sold the portfolio four years later for a $30,000 profit, proving his philosophy that "the time of maximum pessimism is the best time to buy." Templeton's investment strategy, emphasizing buying during low sentiment, sizing positions to mitigate risk, and holding long-term, made him one of the wealthiest men globally and defined his successful career, leading to the creation of the Templeton Growth Fund.
